title: Exercises in any language (C first): review
intro_html: The staged change from plans/2026-10-23-c-exercises.md; uv run pytest: 1050 passed, integration included.
summary_html:
The idea. Exercises used a bundled Python harness to drop input() prompts, match exceptions by class hierarchy and report the line. That made every other language a special case. Now an exercise program runs exactly as a challenge submission does, Language.compile then Language.run, and what differs between languages is a key in languages.toml (env, error_name, editor_mode), not a branch in Python.

Behaviour changes to review: prompts are output; error: matches a name exactly (no subclasses); a failure's name comes from the signal or from the language's error_name regex over stderr; a failed compile is a result of its own, not N failing tests; a session cannot switch language. Old stored results are folded into the new shape on read: no migration.

Not done: npm run build:css (no node_modules here); deployed sets built by the harness may need prompts and base-class error blocks fixed before re-import. Step 1 was a spike (no code; results in the plan).

cocco/languages.py.comment_html:
New module holding the data of a languages.toml entry, with no execution, so format.py and the web process read names, extensions and editor_mode without importing the judge (isolate, nix, the database). LanguageSpec type-checks the three new optional keys on load and compiles error_name so a bad regex fails at startup, not at the first student's run.

Review: load_languages(path, cls=) with a TypeVar lets the judge build its executable subclass from the same loader. The type: ignore on the default cls is the price of that; the alternative was a second loader.

cocco/languages.toml.comment_html:
The language-specific bits, as data:
  • [python] env: PYTHONHASHSEED=0, what the deleted EXERCISE_ENV did (a set prints in the same order in the solution's box and the student's). Challenges get it too; it only makes a run reproducible.
  • [python] error_name: the spike's adjusted regex. The name line must follow an indented line (a frame, source or caret line), so a multi-line exception message or sys.exit('bye') no longer yields a bogus name. Linear-time; the (?:[ \t]+.*\n)+ variant was quadratic and hung.
  • [c]: -Wall (warnings shown collapsed in exercises; a challenge shows compiler output only on failure, checked) and -lm last, where the linker needs it (without it sqrt(x) fails to link; costs ~15 ms).
  • editor_mode on every entry, CodeMirror's mode/MIME.

cocco/judge.py.comment_html: Most of the change. Touched in steps 2, 3, 4 and 5; the notes on each hunk say which. Read in this order: read_exercise_run (the mapping table), prepare_exercise_program / run_exercise_program (the whole per-language surface, no if language ==), _check_compiled, run_exercise_job, build_exercise.

cocco/test_languages.py.comment_html: Loading defaults, the bundled entries' values, the Python error_name on a real traceback shape, rejection of bad types/regexes, and one integration test that run sets the env in the box and honours fsize_kb.

cocco/web/core.py.comment_html: Step 2: imports load_languages from cocco.languages (the web no longer needs the judge for this). Step 9: editor_mode(language), the one lookup templates need; "" means plain text for a language without the key.

cocco/test_judge.py.comment_html: Synthetic meta-file parsing (clean exit, RE with exitcode:3, SG with exitsig:11) plus one integration test with real Python programs dying of SIGSEGV and exiting 3.

cocco/schema.py.comment_html:
• HarnessReport, HarnessException, MAX_EXCEPTION_LINE gone.
  • ExerciseExecution.error: str | None replaces exception; no line (only the harness knew it; the stderr shown on visible tests names the line itself).
  • _fold_old_exception (mode="before"): an old stored row's exception.type becomes error and its traceback is appended to stderr. No migration: every old row still validates through EXERCISE_JOB_RESULT. no_report stays in the literal for the same reason, though nothing produces it now.
  • ExerciseCompile(ok, diagnostics), optional on check and run results (None for interpreted languages and every older row).

Review: the validator drops mro; old rows were graded already, so nothing re-reads it.

cocco/exercises/harness.py.comment_html: Deleted. Every program, Python included, now runs as Language.run runs it.

cocco/exercises/__init__.py.comment_html: HARNESS_PATH and the paragraph about the harness go.

cocco/test_exercise_judge.py.comment_html:
Changed only where a test pinned harness semantics; everything else passes as it was:
  • prompts: test_a_prompt_is_output (a prompt now fails a check; a Run shows it in stdout, stdin not echoed);
  • error: ArithmeticError → ZeroDivisionError in SOURCE, and a test that LookupError no longer matches IndexError;
  • os._exit(0) is a normal exit (the program flushes first; unflushed output is lost, as it would be anywhere);
  • harness-report parsing tests removed; 11 unit tests on synthetic RunOutcomes, one per row of the mapping, including the Python flood (RE, exit 120, OSError, stdout at the cap → truncated, not error=OSError);
  • old-shape stored check/run results validate (step 4), a compile result round-trips.

cocco/test_exercise_routes.py.comment_html: Fixtures use error / stderr instead of exception; step 9 drops the one prompt from SOURCE.

cocco/test_exercise_student.py.comment_html: Hidden tests: the redacted row now carries error (a name HINTS knows, else "error"); a hidden SIGSEGV is shown by name. test_a_forged_line_is_no_line removed: there is no line any more.

cocco/exercises/format.py.comment_html:
• language: front-matter key, checked against languages.toml at import (a C file read as Python would build every solution into a SyntaxError, and the build is the slow place to find out). linguaggio joins _ITALIAN.
  • Fence prefixes come from the entry: name or any extension (py starter still works; cc solution in a C++ file).
  • <other language> <role> (python solution in a C file) is an error naming the right spelling: left alone it would be statement text, solution and all. A bare ```c block stays statement text.
  • error block: one word, [A-Za-z_][\w.]*, so SIGFPE and json.decoder.JSONDecodeError both pass. Whether the language can produce it is the build's to discover.

Review: after an unknown language the parse carries on with the first entry only to avoid an error cascade; the document is discarded anyway because the problem is an error.

cocco/test_exercise_c.py.comment_html: 16 tests; no production change was needed, which is the point of this step. Check: hello world, compile error (tests=[], main.c:2), warning kept with ok=True, SIGFPE (via a / b read from stdin: gcc folds 1/z at -O2), timeout, flood, return 3, #include of a host file does not compile. Run: assert → SIGABRT, stdout shown, non-compiling run. Build: non-compiling solution is an error, starter a warning, error: ValueError in C fails naming SIGSEGV.

cocco/exercises/hints.py.comment_html: Signal hints (SIGSEGV, SIGFPE, SIGABRT, SIGBUS, SIGILL, SIGXCPU); error_hint loses line. One dict: names cannot collide across languages in practice.

cocco/test_exercise_compare.py.comment_html: error_hint tests for the new signature, plus a signal.

cocco/web/exercise_sets.py.comment_html: _builtin_exception_name → _shown_error_name: the name if it is a key of HINTS, else "error". Same bound as before (a program picks its own exception or signal name, e.g. a class named after the hidden input, so only a fixed list is shown) and language-neutral. The redacted row now carries a plain error string. Step 9: the preview route passes language / editor_mode.

cocco/repository/exercise_sessions.py.comment_html: query_version_language (coalesced to python for documents that predate the key), the session's versions CTE carries language, and (step 9) the sessions list and query_session_job select it / stdin.

cocco/web/exercise_sessions.py.comment_html:
The switch guard: refused when the new version's language differs from the pinned one's. The existing guards were never one SQL statement, they are sequential reads under the session's FOR UPDATE lock, so the language check joins them there. _version_switch shows the same refusal on the page instead of the Switch button. Step 9: drill-in and projector pass language to highlight.

cocco/test_exercise_sessions.py.comment_html: Python-pinned session, C version imported: no switch button, the POST is 200 with the alert, the session stays put.

cocco/web/exercise_student.py.comment_html: The student page passes language and editor_mode, read from the pinned version.

cocco/templates/f-exercise-job.jinja.comment_html:
Steps 4, 8 and 9:
  • compile_notes: a failed compile is an alert plus the diagnostics (shown in full even where tests are redacted: it is about the student's own source, no stdin involved); warnings are collapsed above the tests.
  • A failed check compile shows only that block (no "0 of 0 passed").
  • "Standard error" → "Error output" (the traceback lives there now); "Input given" above a Run's transcript, since stdin is no longer echoed.
  • Redacted rows: row.error, with no hint when the name is the generic "error" (avoids "error — Error error.").

cocco/templates/f-exercise-set.jinja.comment_html: Language badge, only once the latest version is ready (a building one has no document and would read python).

cocco/web/seed.py.comment_html: A three-exercise C set on the first course (pass with a wrong-output starter, a % b → SIGFPE, assert → SIGABRT), seeded as an import leaves it: a building version plus a build job, so it becomes ready once a judge runs. The seed had no Python sets, so no prompts to remove.

cocco/judge.py: from cocco.languages import
Step 2: the data and the loader come from cocco.languages; judge re-exports what it used to define so cj.language_for_filename keeps working.
def _parse_meta
Step 3: the meta parsing pulled out as a pure function so it is unit-testable without isolate. retcode is isolate's own (1 for RE/SG, 0 becomes 127) and was never the program's status.
class Language(LanguageSpec)
Step 2: Language keeps only compile / run; its fields live on LanguageSpec.
fsize_kb=fsize_kb
Step 2: run passes fsize_kb and the entry's env in both branches; None leaves challenge behaviour unchanged.
EXERCISE_FSIZE_KB = 256
The output cap moves from the harness (256 K characters) to isolate (256 KB): past it a C program dies of SIGXFSZ, Python fails to write.
def read_exercise_run

The mapping, in this order: XX raises (judge error); TO; OOM; truncated (SIGXFSZ, or a stream at the cap by encoded length; before RE because Python exits 120 with OSError instead of dying); OK; RE named by the language's error_name; any other signal named by signal.Signals (unknown → SIG<n>), exit 128+n. Output goes through _jsonb_safe first, so what is compared is what is stored.

Accepted cost: a program writing exactly 256 KB and exiting cleanly reads as truncated.
def prepare_exercise_program
The whole per-language surface: write main.<ext>, compile; then run once per stdin. One compile per check, never one per test.
def _compile_report
compile is filled whenever the language has a compiler (not a C feature), capped at MAX_EXERCISE_STORED_OUTPUT.
def error_matches
Exact name equality: no MRO without a harness. Settled in the plan; the loss is accepted.
def _check_compiled
A source that does not compile ran nothing: passed=False, tests=[]. Split out so the build can grade the starter on an already-compiled program.
def exercise_language
Replaces _python: refuses only a name languages.toml lacks (the parse already checked; this is the judge not trusting a stored document).
def _compile_detail
Added in review: a failed compile's diagnostics for a build problem, from the head (gcc's first error is the useful one), unlike _detail which keeps a stderr's tail.
solution_dir = workdir / "solution"

Solution and starter each compile once, in their own subdirectory (the hardcoded solution.py goes). A solution that does not compile is an error with the diagnostics; a starter that does not, a warning (a gap to fill may be deliberate).

Kept as before: an empty error block with a solution that fails without a name (return 3) is a build error. Allowing it would need grade to represent "any failure".
